hypothesis: A calibrated paraxial ABCD model will reproduce OpticStudio paraxial ray-trace retinal edges to numerical precision, while source angular extent controls focused coverage and pupil diameter controls defocus blur.
limitations: No absolute radiometry or retinal safety conclusion is possible without source flux, exposure, spectrum, and tissue transmission data.
The current eyes are effective paraxial thin-lens models and do not include anatomical surfaces, aberrations, scattering, or eye rotation.
The slide-5 15 D lens was interpreted as -15 D, and external-lens vertex distances are provisional assumptions.
next_step: Replace each effective eye with a multi-surface anatomical model, add measured radiometry and vertex distances, then perform non-sequential stray-light and tolerance Monte Carlo validation.
objective: Determine the circular 650 nm source geometry required to illuminate specified posterior-pole regions in chick, child, and adult effective-eye models, quantify defocus and external-lens sensitivity, and cross-validate with licensed OpticStudio ray tracing.
observations: Focused physical source diameter scales inversely with object vergence magnitude while the required angular diameter stays close to 20 degrees.
The chick 20 D and adult 20 D conditions exceed the accommodation limits supplied in the source presentation.
At 100 mm object distance, the adult model remains feasible through a -10 D external lens but exceeds its 18 D accommodation limit at -15 D and -20 D.
Pupil diameter does not change the ideal focused source image size in the paraxial model, but it linearly increases geometric defocus blur.
Five focused OpticStudio systems and one intentionally unaccommodated system agree with the independent model to double-precision numerical tolerance.
